A1.justification: Both complete 27-page PDFs describe the same URSA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching renamed models and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original URSA and URSA-RM benchmark results, test-time sampling experiments, ablations, and case studies, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds Math-Vision evaluation and component-specific CoT synthesis ablations.

M1.justification: The SAM-B/SigLIP-L vision tower, MLP projector, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct backbone, CoT synthesis procedures, and dual-view PRM remain the same. The 7B-to-8B relabeling and revised description of response filtering do not establish a changed architecture or algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds Math-Vision, covering difficult mathematical problems across 16 competencies, including combinatorics and topology, for direct reasoning, test-time scaling, and ablation evaluation. MathVista, MathVerse, WE-MATH, DYNAMATH, and GeoQA are retained; GeoQA was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: V3 adds LLaVA-OneVision and InternVL2.5-8B to retained benchmark comparisons and supplies MathVerse comparisons for GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5-Flash-002 where v1 had no scores. Math-Vision also introduces comparators such as Ovis1.6-Gemma2-9B and MiniCPM-v2.6. These update the existing broad MLLM comparison suite; the self-consistency control remains.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Table 6 revise the reported alignment-training volume from 960K to 860K without establishing whether training was rerun. New component ablations replace individual synthesized subsets with original data while preserving total SFT data volume (Figure 7). Other stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds separate ablations of answer-only distillation, analysis rewriting, and CoT format unification across five benchmarks (Figure 7). V1's aggregate augmentation-versus-original-data experiments are retained and merged into appendix Figure 8. Both PRM-component ablations and the case studies already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains its shaded-band reporting style, extended to the new Math-Vision panel. V3 adds no explanation of these bands, repeated-run or random-seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance testing. Candidate-sampling budgets are distinct from repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 adds Math-Vision scores, including URSA accuracy 26.2 (Table 10) and Best-of-8 accuracy 32.6 (Figure 6), plus component-ablation results. Table 1 revises GPT-4V's MathVerse overall score from 54.4 to 39.4; Table 5 changes the no-misinterpretation ablation's MathVista-GPS score at N=64 from 85.6 to 83.6. These are added or revised reported results; retained URSA benchmark and OOD scores remain stable.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same dataset definitions and training losses, and Algorithm 1 retains the same binary error-location procedure. No theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: V3 newly calls DualMath-1.1M the first process-supervised dataset for multimodal mathematical reasoning and expands headline performance claims to six benchmarks and verifier-guided reasoning surpassing GPT-4o. The central dataset, reasoning-model, and verifier contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds component-specific explanations linking distillation to accuracy, rewriting to WE-MATH reasoning, and textual diversity to robustness. Section 5.2 adds a limitation about problem-specific misinterpretation prompts. V1's explicit warning about verifier saturation as N increases is removed, and Appendix C.3 adds interpretations of Math-Vision subject balance.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies zero-shot reasoning, rule-based answer matching for five benchmarks, and GPT-4o extraction/evaluation for MathVerse (Section 4.1 and Appendix B). It also supplies benchmark sample counts and replaces the future open-source promise with repository access information. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified evaluation procedures.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations for SAM, SigLIP, InternVL2.5, Ovis, and Math-Vision, removes the GeoGPT4V discussion and several citations, and strengthens the dataset-priority claim. The related-work framing around multimodal mathematics and inference-time scaling is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, related work, and several methodological and interpretive passages are extensively rewritten. System 2 terminology and 8B model names are adopted throughout much of the document, and the appendices are reorganized with a new evaluation section and subdivided supplementary results.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the two skill/modality radar charts with a six-benchmark overview. Figure 6 becomes a three-panel scaling comparison; v3 adds a component-ablation figure and Math-Vision table. The original augmentation plots are merged and relocated to appendix Figure 8, alongside substantial figure and table reflow.

improvement.justification: The component-specific ablations directly test design choices that v1 evaluated only as a bundle, while Math-Vision extends validation to harder and broader mathematics. Added scoring and access information improve transparency. These gains are limited by unexplained alignment-data and ablation-score revisions and broader SOTA wording despite Table 1 placing InternVL2.5 above URSA on MathVista.
